translations.en: Ṣabbāḥ ibn Yaḥyā, al-Muzannī, Abū Muḥammad, Kufan. Zaydi. His ḥadīth is in

chunks.arabic_text: حَدِيثِ أَصْحَابِنَا، ضَعِيفٌ، جَوَازٌ أَنْ يُخْرَجَ شَاهِدًا.

translations.en: the ḥadīth of our companions. Weak. It is permissible for him to be brought out as a witness.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghada'iri's *Kitab al-Du'afa* characterizes Ṣabbāḥ ibn Yaḥyā al-Muzannī as a Kufan Zaydi narrator whose hadith, while deemed weak (da'if) for independent legal proof, is acceptable as a corroborating witness (shahid). This classification reflects the Shia scholarly nuance of distinguishing between primary evidentiary strength and secondary supportive value, particularly when evaluating narrators from different theological sects like the Zaydis.
en.seo_question: What is the status of Ṣabbāḥ ibn Yaḥyā's narrations in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.زَيْدِيٌّ: Zaydi (referring to the Zaydi Shia sect)
key_terms.أَصْحَابِنَا: Our companions (referring to prominent Shia jurists/narrators)
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Weak (a technical term for a narrator whose reliability is not high enough for independent proof)
key_terms.شَاهِدًا: As a witness/supporting evidence (shahid, used for weak narrations that corroborate stronger ones)
